events.title: Dollar Eases Again Toward G. 6,000 as Exporters Press BCP for Intervention (2026-08-21)
events.summary: The US dollar closed the week of August 21 at G. 6,010 in the retail market and G. 6,009 at the interbank level, again approaching the G. 6,000 threshold after touching G. 5,950 two weeks earlier. The guaraní's sustained appreciation — roughly 20% over the past year — is eroding dollar-linked revenue, prompting exporters, led by the cattle and agricultural sectors, to demand that the Central Bank (BCP) intervene to 'balance' the market. The BCP has so far maintained a hands-off stance.

events.title: CEPAL Projects Paraguay to Grow 4.3% in 2026, Among South America's Most Dynamic (2026-08-20)
events.summary: The UN Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean (CEPAL) projects Paraguay's economy will grow 4.3% in 2026, keeping it among South America's most dynamic economies, ahead of the regional average. The forecast aligns closely with the IMF and World Bank (4.4%) and the BCP's own upgraded estimate of 4.5%, reflecting sustained strength in agriculture, manufacturing and services. CEPAL also sees Paraguay growing around 4.0% in 2027.

events.title: Economist Proposes Raising Public Debt Ceiling to 70% of GDP for Development (2026-08-19)
events.summary: A leading Paraguayan economist argued that the country should raise its public debt ceiling to 70% of GDP to finance infrastructure and development, well above the current legal framework which caps debt near 40% of GDP under the Fiscal Responsibility Law. Proponents contend that Paraguay's low debt load and investment-grade trajectory give it ample fiscal space, while critics warn that loosening the anchor could jeopardize the hard-won macroeconomic credibility that underpins cheap financing.

events.title: Beef Sector: Export Price Up 21% but Volume Down 25% Amid Strong Guaraní (2026-08-20)
events.summary: Paraguay's cattle sector faces a classic currency squeeze: average beef export prices rose from about USD 4,500 to USD 6,900–7,000 per tonne (peaking near USD 7,500 in July), but export volumes fell 25%. The higher prices (+21%) only partially offset the volume decline, leaving foreign-exchange earnings down roughly 9%. The United States has become the top destination, followed by Israel and Taiwan, while the 9.9% seven-month depreciation of the dollar against the guaraní has compressed producer margins.

events.title: Energy Reform Advances: Bill to Split ANDE into Six Companies Presented (2026-08-21)
events.summary: Senator Enrique Salyn Buzarquis presented a 'General Electricity Industry Law' that would split state utility ANDE into six separate companies and create a Superintendency of Electricity. The proposal runs parallel to the executive's own reform — creating a Ministry of Energy, Mines and Hydrocarbons plus an independent regulator — reflecting a broad consensus that the sector must be restructured. The bill is slated for debate as electricity demand grows more than 18% annually versus ANDE's 10% projection.

events.title: Peña Promulgates JICA Loan of USD 224M for the Yabebyry–Pilar Road Corridor (2026-08-21)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña promulgated Law No. 7713, approving a JICA loan of up to ¥36.38 billion (about USD 224 million) to improve the Yabebyry–Pilar corridor, a road project executed by the Ministry of Public Works (MOPC). The financing deepens Japan's role in Paraguayan infrastructure and complements the ongoing Japanese bilateral agenda, including beef market access and the 90th anniversary of Japanese immigration.

events.title: Executive Authorizes G. 73.7B in PGN 2026 Modifications via 14 Decrees (2026-08-22)
events.summary: The executive issued 14 decrees (No. 6581–6662) authorizing modifications to the 2026 national budget (PGN 2026): increases of G. 59,302 million and reprogramming of G. 14,404.8 million, totaling G. 73,707 million (about USD 12.2 million). Funds were directed to health, the Ministry of Finance, MITIC, social development, agriculture, labor, defense, the anti-drug secretariat (Senad), the Boquerón governorate and the National University of Asunción, among others.

events.title: Doctors Ratify Five-Day National Strike for August 24–28 (2026-08-22)
events.summary: The National Doctors Union (SINAMED) ratified a five-day national strike from August 24–28 after negotiations with the government broke down. Scheduled consultations and elective surgeries in public hospitals will be suspended, while emergency and essential services remain guaranteed. Doctors demand a G. 3,000,000 salary adjustment per post, double pay for holidays worked, and the regularisation (deprecarización) of precarious contracts, noting they have had no wage increase for 12 years.

events.title: Government Formalizes Appointment of 11,000 Health Workers Ahead of Strike (2026-08-21)
events.summary: Facing the looming doctors' strike, the government formalized the appointment of roughly 11,000 health-sector workers — 9,755 medical staff (doctors, dentists, biochemists, nurses, technicians and auxiliaries) plus 1,345 administrative positions. The move is part of a broader effort to 'deprecarizar' (convert precarious contracts into permanent posts) the public health workforce and defuse labor unrest, though unions say salary and conditions demands remain unmet.

events.title: Nurses Secure 7,000 Permanent Posts in Labor Regularization Push (2026-08-21)
events.summary: The Paraguayan Nursing Association reached agreement with authorities to create 7,000 permanent posts, advancing the deprecarización of nursing staff. Beneficiaries will move to salary level 1 (about G. 4.3 million), a significant step toward formalizing a workforce that has long relied on short-term contracts. The agreement is part of a broader government drive to regularize public-health employment amid rising social and labor tensions.

events.title: Japan's Crown Prince Akishino and Princess Kiko Begin Official Visit to Paraguay (2026-08-21)
events.summary: Crown Prince Akishino and Princess Kiko of Japan began an official visit to Paraguay to mark the 90th anniversary of Japanese immigration, laying a wreath at the National Pantheon of Heroes alongside Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano. The visit underscores the deep historical ties between the two countries and the Japanese community's economic and social weight in Paraguay, and coincides with a push to open the Japanese market to Paraguayan beef.

events.title: Peña and Japanese Minister Kiuchi Advance Beef Market Access Agenda (2026-08-22)
events.summary: President Santiago Peña met with Japanese State Minister Minoru Kiuchi to advance access for Paraguayan beef to the Japanese market, alongside discussions on investment and defense and security cooperation. Japan, a high-value beef importer, is a strategic target for Paraguayan meat exporters seeking to diversify beyond current markets and capture premium prices, complementing the JICA infrastructure financing already in place.

events.title: Mercosur–EU: No Deal on Beef Export Quotas; Paraguay Holds Out for 25% (2026-08-19)
events.summary: Mercosur members have yet to agree on how to distribute the beef export quotas under the Mercosur–EU trade agreement, with Paraguay insisting on an equitable 25% share for each member state, a position backed by producer unions (ARP, CPC, Capeco, UGP). Without consensus, the existing 'first-come, first-served' system would remain in place and the issue would be revisited in October 2027, leaving uncertainty over a key export channel for Paraguayan ranchers.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI

events.title: HIVE: Columbia Validates Paraguay AI GPUs; 100 MW Substation Energization Set for September (2026-08-18)
events.summary: HIVE Digital Technologies completed its first AI research trial using GPUs in Asunción, in collaboration with Columbia University's Department of Industrial Engineering and Operations Research — researchers in New York remotely ran iterative AI training on GPUs over 5,000 miles away, a proof of concept for intercontinental AI compute. The study found HIVE's Nvidia A40 GPUs matched newer-generation H100 performance after optimization and was submitted to NeurIPS. The company's 100 MW substation at its Yguazú 'Gigafactory' is complete, with energization targeted for September 2026 and Tier III data-center construction starting in autumn.
events.client_tag: HIVE — AI/HPC data center, 100 MW substation, GPU compute

events.title: Atome Defends 2022 ANDE PPA, Announces Study for a 300 MWp Solar Plant (2026-08-19)
events.summary: Atome, an energy company, defended its power purchase agreement (PPA) with ANDE in force since 2022 for 145 MW of reserved capacity — which it says is already incorporated into the state utility's projections to 2050 — and announced studies for a 300 MWp solar plant. The announcement highlights the growing queue of private energy projects (over 6,000 MW) awaiting clear rules as the government's electricity reform advances and ANDE's list of potential customers becomes dominated by AI and data-center operators.
events.client_tag: Atome — 145 MW PPA, 300 MWp solar; energy-sector reform

events.title: Riquelme Courts Chile for Energy Exports and AI Data Centers (2026-08-20)
events.summary: Industry and Commerce Minister Marco Riquelme traveled to Chile at President Peña's request to attract investment, focused on exporting Paraguayan energy, regional electricity interconnection and AI data centers. The visit ties Paraguay's clean-energy surplus to the Bioceanic Corridor and positions the country as a potential energy supplier to Chile, a key partner. It also supports the government's legislative push to open the electricity market to private generation.
events.client_tag: Digital energy — regional interconnection, AI data centers

events.title: Tigo (Millicom): Q2 2026 — Paraguay Posts Group-Leading 56.9% EBITDA Margin (2026-08-06)
events.summary: Millicom (Tigo) reported record Q2 2026 results: group service revenue of USD 2.0 billion (+5% organic), record adjusted EBITDA of USD 1.0 billion (46.3% margin) and record equity free cash flow of USD 327 million. Paraguay contributed 8% of group service revenue (USD 169 million, +3.4% organic) and posted the group's highest adjusted EBITDA margin at 56.9%, boosted by the guaraní's appreciation which lowered the dollar cost of content and sports rights. Management flagged the FX-driven margin as potentially unsustainable if the currency reverses.
events.client_tag: Millicom/Tigo — 5G 2.3 GHz deployment; network equipment, base stations

events.title: Personal (Telecom Argentina): H1 Capex Up 47.3% to USD 631M; FTTH Now 36% of Base (2026-08-14)
events.summary: Telecom Argentina (Personal) accelerated capital expenditure in H1 2026 to ARS 946.47 billion (about USD 631 million), up 47.3% year-on-year and equivalent to 18.6% of consolidated sales, toward a full-year target of up to USD 1.3 billion. Investment is directed at fixed and mobile data, 4G site modernization, 5G deployment and FTTH fiber, with FTTH now 36% of the broadband base (over 1.5 million connections). In Paraguay, subsidiary Núcleo (Personal) holds two 3.7 GHz lots and leads the FTTH market with 1.66 million mobile users.
events.client_tag: Telecom Argentina/Personal — 5G 3.7 GHz deployment; FTTH, fiber

events.title: Nubicom: USD 200M Standalone 5G Rollout with Ericsson and Nokia Advances (2026-08-15)
events.summary: Argentina's Nubicom is advancing what it calls the largest 5G deployment in Paraguay, a roughly USD 200 million standalone (5G SA) network after winning 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band, with technology partners cited as Ericsson and Nokia. The operator, which established local subsidiary Nubicom Paraguay, must deploy at least 100 base stations per 100 MHz awarded (200 base stations total) and is a test case for new-entrant viability in a market dominated by Tigo, Personal and Claro.
events.client_tag: Nubicom — 5G SA rollout; Ericsson/Nokia equipment opportunity

events.title: Claro: First 5G Network (Nokia) Expands as FTTH Edge Modules Add Capacity (2026-08-15)
events.summary: Claro (América Móvil) continues to operate Paraguay's first commercial 5G network, activated in December 2025 with Nokia equipment and an initial USD 35 million investment, now covering Greater Asunción, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación, Coronel Oviedo and Pedro Juan Caballero. Datawaves' modular edge data-center and FTTH modules have expanded Claro's fiber capacity, positioning it to scale 5G services as demand grows, while it serves 947,000 mobile users — the smallest of the three major operators.
events.client_tag: América Móvil/Claro — 5G expansion, FTTH, edge data center

sections.title: VII. Integrated Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.impact_analysis:
🟡 FX Pressure — Strong Guaraní Squeezes Exporters, Benefits Importers: The dollar's renewed slide toward G. 6,000 (G. 6,009 interbank on Aug 21) is the week's defining macro theme. For importers of capital goods and telecom/energy equipment, the strong guaraní lowers landed costs and boosts purchasing power. For exporters — cattle, soy and maquila — it compresses guaraní margins, visible in beef's 25% volume drop despite a 21% price rise. Businesses with USD-denominated revenue should maintain hedging, echoing the BCP's push on forward contracts.

🟢 Growth Momentum Intact: CEPAL's 4.3% projection for 2026, corroborated by the IMF/World Bank (4.4%) and the BCP (4.5%), confirms Paraguay remains one of the region's fastest-growing economies. Strong domestic demand and diversification into manufacturing and services support telecom and digital-infrastructure demand, though growth is still anchored in agriculture.

🔴 Labor & Social Risk — Health Sector Strike: The five-day national doctors' strike (Aug 24–28) and the government's parallel appointment of 11,000 health workers signal acute social tension despite solid macro numbers. The IPS crisis and precarización demands mirror the broader discontent seen in prior weeks' protests. Firms with public-facing operations or health-sector contracts should plan for service disruptions this week.

🟢 Structural Energy Reform — Long-Term Opportunity: The parallel bills to split ANDE into six companies and create a Ministry of Energy, Mines and Hydrocarbons plus an independent regulator mark the most consequential policy shift of the period. With demand growing 18% annually and over 6,000 MW of private projects queued, the reform promises clearer rules for data centers and AI operators (HIVE, the Taiwan Yguazú Digital hub). The 100 MW HIVE substation energization in September is a concrete near-term milestone.

🟡 Client Diversification & FX Sensitivity: Millicom's disclosure that Paraguay's 56.9% EBITDA margin was partly FX-driven (and 'potentially unsustainable') is a reminder that operator profitability in Paraguay is currency-sensitive. All four 5G licensees (Claro, Nubicom, Tigo, Personal) remain under deployment deadlines, sustaining near-term equipment demand, but suppliers should diversify across operators and into enterprise/private networks given the concentrated, foreign-controlled market.

sections.title: VIII. Targeted Recommendations for Chinese Enterprises
sections.impact_analysis:
🔴 High Risk — Diplomatic Constraints Unchanged: Paraguay remains Taiwan's sole South American ally, and no diplomatic thaw with Beijing occurred this week. Chinese enterprises should continue to expect exclusion from public 5G and infrastructure tenders — the trusted-vendor rules bar Huawei and ZTE, a constraint reaffirmed by the second 5G auction — and must run rigorous compliance reviews before any Paraguay-linked engagement.

🟡 Medium Risk — Indirect Access Only: China remains Paraguay's largest goods supplier (phones, computers, tires), and Chinese firms can still serve the market indirectly through Brazilian, Argentine or Chilean subsidiaries or trading intermediaries. The Japan-Paraguay beef agenda and Mercosur-EU quota talks are regional channels to monitor, but direct Chinese-branded deals in sensitive sectors (telecom, energy) stay politically constrained.

🟢 Opportunity — Energy & Digital Infrastructure: The electricity reform (ANDE split, Ministry of Energy, independent regulator) and the 18%-annual demand growth create demand for power equipment, transmission and grid modernization where Chinese suppliers (transformers, HVDC, solar modules) can participate through consortiums with non-Chinese partners. Atome's 300 MWp solar study and the 6,000 MW project queue signal concrete procurement opportunities.

🟢 Opportunity — Equipment via Third Parties: The 5G buildout — Nubicom's USD 200 million standalone network with Ericsson/Nokia, plus Tigo and Personal deployment deadlines — requires radios, fiber and edge infrastructure. Chinese equipment vendors, though barred from public auctions, can pursue enterprise/private networks, wholesale fiber, and partnerships with Latin American integrators (Datawaves-style suppliers) already serving Claro, Tigo and Personal.

🟡 Caution — Labor & FX Risk: The doctors' strike, IPS crisis and persistent precarización point to labor friction despite headline growth; the strong guaraní (about 20% appreciation over a year) simultaneously erodes the renminbi value of any USD-linked revenue. Chinese firms with local operations should review labor compliance, plan around this week's health-sector strike, and hedge FX exposure proactively.
